title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, with standard loops l_0, l_1, l_infinity satisfying l_0 l_infinity l_1 = 1 (as used on the next page). Its profinite completion is written pi^_{0,3}. It sits inside the profinite completion O^_{0,3} (or G^_{0,3}) of the extension by the symmetric group G_3 = S_3. That group S_3 is generated by an involution sigma_infinity and a 3-cycle rho, which permute the loops cyclically: rho(l_0) = l_infinity, and so on. The positive part G^+_{0,3} is the extension

 1 -> pi^_{0,3} -> G^+_{0,3} -> Z/3 -> 1,

whose quotient Z/3 is generated by the image of rho.

Theorem 327 (previous pages) describes the outer automorphisms u commuting with the S_3-action. These are given by u(rho) = g rho and u(l_0) = int(g_0) l_0^beta, with an exponent beta in Z^ and an element g_0 in pi^_{0,3}. These are essentially the Drinfeld–Ihara data (lambda, f) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^.

The Scholie makes three points.
(i) The quantities x and g that enter directly into writing u can be expressed through g_0, which determines L_0, and through gamma = (p-1)/2. This exponent plays the role of Drinfeld's m = (lambda-1)/2.
(ii) The remaining condition (46) is really a condition on g_0 alone. It is cleanest in terms of xi = l_0^gamma h_0^{-1}, so that h_0 = xi^{-1} l_0^gamma.
(iii) Condition (46) reads xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1, which is (51). Since rho^3 = 1 and rho(x) = rho x rho^{-1}, one has (xi rho)^3 = xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) rho^3. Hence (51) is equivalent to (52), (xi rho)^3 = 1. This is the cyclic, 'hexagon/triangle' relation of GT.

Grothendieck then reinterprets this cohomologically.
- Solutions xi correspond bijectively to splittings of the Z/3-extension G^+_{0,3}, that is, to elements of order 3 lying above rho. Equivalently, they are 1-cocycles of Z/3 with values in pi^_{0,3}, the action being conjugation by rho.
- pi^_{0,3} acts on these splittings by inner automorphisms, as in (53): int(lambda)(xi rho) = (lambda xi rho(lambda)^{-1}) rho.
- On the solutions of (51) this is the twisted conjugation (54): xi |-> lambda xi rho(lambda)^{-1}, i.e. the coboundary action.
- The NB states that lambda |-> ^lambda xi is injective, i.e. the action is free. Equivalently, the centralizer in pi^_{0,3} of the order-3 element xi rho is trivial.

So the solution set of the cyclic GT relation becomes a torsor-union over the nonabelian cohomology set H^1(Z/3, pi^_{0,3}), the set of conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts of rho.

The next page assumes that H^1 has exactly two classes:
- the coboundaries xi = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1}, the tautological solutions;
- the class of l_1^{-1} ~ l_0^{-1}, coming from the other order-3 element sigma_infinity rho^{-1} sigma_infinity.
It then solves case by case, giving h_0 = rho(lambda) lambda^{-1} l_0^gamma. This is a structural route to describing elements of GT^ through classification of finite subgroups in profinite completions of virtually free (orbifold) groups.
errors: No mathematical error is visible in (51)<->(52) or in (53)/(54).

The NB (freeness of the action) is asserted without proof. It needs the triangle element xi rho to have trivial centralizer in pi^_{0,3}. This holds discretely (Fuchsian/orbifold group) and in the profinite completion by goodness/torsion results, but that is nontrivial and is not argued here.

The key input used on the next page — exactly two conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts — is explicitly only 'admitted' ('Admettons, quitte à le vérifier'). It is the profinite analogue of the classification of torsion in a virtually free group and requires e.g. Ribes–Zalesskii-type results.

ideas.what: Rewriting the cyclic (hexagon) condition on the GT-data as xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1, with xi = l_0^gamma h_0^{-1} and gamma = (exponent-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon/3-cycle relation of GT^ (Drinfeld's relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1, m = (lambda-1)/2)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the fundamental group of the Teichmüller tower and S_3-symmetry, but not this explicit formula

ideas.what: Equivalence of the cyclic relation with (xi rho)^3 = 1, so solutions are splittings / order-3 lifts of rho in the Z/3-extension of pi^_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Order-3 element condition; nonabelian H^1(Z/3, pi^_{0,3})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Drinfeld/Ihara; made explicit in Lochak–Schneps and Schneps surveys via PSL_2(Z^)-type actions

ideas.what: Twisted conjugation action xi -> lambda xi rho(lambda)^{-1} of pi^_{0,3} on the solutions, claimed to be free
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary action on 1-cocycles; trivial centralizer of torsion elements in profinite completions of Fuchsian groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard nonabelian cohomology (Serre); freeness via results on centralizers in profinite virtually free groups (Herfort–Ribes–Zalesskii)

ideas.what: Strategy of classifying GT-type data by conjugacy classes of finite-order lifts (two classes: tautological, and that of l_1^{-1})
ideas.modern_name: Classification of finite subgroups in profinite completions of virtually free groups, applied to GT

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently (in the Longue Marche follow-up notes) reformulates the 3-cycle relation of GT^ as a splitting / nonabelian H^1(Z/3, pi^_{0,3}) problem, with a free twisted-conjugation action. Here this is a structural, cohomological organisation of the GT relations rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Les solutions de l'équation (51), ou ce qui revient au même de (52), correspondent aux scindages de l'extension G^+_{0,3} de Z/3Z par pi^_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority/perspective point: it parallels the later Lochak–Schneps treatment of the GT relations via torsion in PSL_2(Z^)-type groups. It is not new mathematics to specialists.

missed.claim: The count of conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts (exactly two) is admitted without proof on the next page.
missed.quote: Admettons (quitte à le vérifier par la suite) qu'il y a exactement deux classes de conjugaison
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is now provable from profinite Bass–Serre theory (Ribes–Zalesskii). It is of no remaining open interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean cohomological reformulation of the GT hexagon relation as order-3 splittings with a free coboundary action. It matches what Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak–Schneps did; it is interesting historically as Grothendieck's own route, but contains nothing a specialist would find unknown.
transcription_corrections: In (51) the image reads xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1 (rho, not g).
gamma = (p-1)/2: the numerator letter is likely the exponent of u(l_0) = int(g_0) l_0^beta, i.e. gamma = (beta-1)/2 or a similar exponent. The letter is unclear.
'x et g (∈ pi^_{0,3}) qui interviennent directement pour écrire u' — the first letter is unclear, possibly a different symbol than x.
In (50) the parenthetical reads 'd'où h_0 = xi^{-1} l_0^gamma'; it is consistent and is the same xi later written zeta on the next page.
